text:
julia-cs: FYI customer 'BrightForms' is seeing weird truncation + nonsense after an APAC failover. They say requests from Tokyo suddenly started returning much shorter replies and strange tokenization (split words mid-token).
julia-cs: They pasted an example: 
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Region: ap-northeast-1
{"model":"redwood-standard-3b","input":"Summarize the policy..."}
```
kevin-support: Are they on Dedicated or Hosted?
julia-cs: Hosted account (free tier => default routing). Customer saw 500ms->50ms latency spike then responses changed. Billing shows token counts dropped by ~60% on those requests.
mike-eng: Strange. 50ms suggests a lightweight variant served. Any chance a standby/lite model was used during failover?
sarah-infra: Our failover policy for ap-northeast-1 will route to standby cluster in us-west-2 if auth probe times out. ops-bot: "region-failover: route switch triggered for ap-northeast-1 -> us-west-2 at 2771112265 (auth probe timeout)" :warning:
lee-ml: If it routed to a quantized/ distilled variant, tokenizer vocab could differ and cause word-splits. Which variant did the logs show?
julia-cs: Customer provided full response headers from the call: 
```
x-rw-model: redwood-lite-v0.9
x-rw-route: standby-us-west-2
x-rw-tokens: 18
x-rw-charges: 0.00012
```
kevin-support: redwood-lite-v0.9 is an older distilled variant — capability delta expected. That explains short outputs + different tokenization. Need to confirm why fallback picked that variant instead of a compatible standby.
mike-eng: Looking at the routing policy: fallback_order for the standard-3b family is [standard-3b, standard-3b-quant, lite-3b]. But standby-us-west-2 only had lite-3b deployed last week due to capacity. That's a config mismatch.
lee-ml: Also, quantized models can have different tokenization if vocab mapping differs. We should repro with an identical input to confirm token boundaries.
sarah-infra: Repro steps I ran: (1) set X-Region: ap-northeast-1, (2) force auth probe failure by blocking probe IP, (3) repeat request. Observed immediate route to standby-us-west-2 and x-rw-model=redwood-lite-v0.9. Paste logs: 
```
[2771112265] probe failed: timeout 1s
[2771112265] route decision -> standby-us-west-2 (available variants: lite-3b)
[2771112266] request served 45ms
```
julia-cs: Customer also reported 401s intermittently before the switch — could be auth probe flapping causing the region to be considered unhealthy.
kevin-support: Action items: (1) Confirm deploy inventory in standby-us-west-2 (which variants live there) (2) Add guardrail to prevent fallback to variants with different tokenizer/vocab for the same model family (3) Contact the customer with repro steps and a compensated credits offer.
mike-eng: I'll open an infra ticket to backfill a compatible standard-3b variant in us-west-2 and add a runtime check: if tokenizer_id != primary.tokenizer_id then avoid that fallback unless explicitly opted-in.
lee-ml: Also add an eval that compares tokenized outputs for a set of canonical prompts when a standby variant is registered. We can auto-block mismatches > 5% token boundary diffs.
sarah-infra: For immediate mitigation I can relax the auth probe sensitivity in ap-northeast-1 while we fix standby inventory — reduces false positives. Ops will need signoff.
julia-cs: I'll tell BrightForms the root cause and send them repro we ran, offer 3 days of credits, and log the SLA incident. Can someone assign the infra ticket and reference this thread? :eyes: 
kevin-support: Assigned ticket INFRA-3987. Linking logs and the customer's request.
mike-eng: Note for postmortem: billing showed token count discrepancy because lite variant uses different bpe mapping and counts subwords differently — need billing note to avoid charge confusion.
julia-cs: Thanks everyone. I'll keep the thread updated with the customer's acceptance of credits and whether the repro matches their experience. :thumbsup:
